title: General amplitude amplification
summary: Amplify a reversible procedure’s success probability by reflecting in its good/bad plane.
why: Shows how Grover extends beyond uniform candidate preparation.
advantage: Proven oracle-model quadratic improvement in preparation/checker calls; total runtime depends on their implementation.

title: Multiple marked items and BBHT search
summary: Randomize iteration lengths when the number of solutions is unknown.
why: Makes overshoot, absence and stopping budgets explicit.
advantage: Proven expected query advantage for unstructured search; bounded-error absence needs a timeout.

title: Fixed-point amplitude amplification
summary: Design selective phases to guarantee a small failure probability over an interval.
why: Connects robust search with polynomial design.
advantage: Proven oracle-model bounded-error quadratic scaling with a valid lower bound; no monotonic-per-gate claim.

title: Dürr–Høyer minimum finding
summary: Find an unsorted table’s minimum by repeatedly searching below a threshold.
why: Demonstrates adaptive classical control around quantum search.
advantage: Proven bounded-error O(sqrt N) value-oracle queries, subject to coherent table/comparison costs.

title: Brassard–Høyer–Tapp collision finding
summary: Trade stored function values for a larger marked set in quantum search.
why: Separates promise collision finding from element distinctness and exposes lookup costs.
advantage: Proven two-to-one oracle-model query/storage tradeoff; gate advantage depends on coherent membership implementation.

title: Quantum Fourier transform and inverse QFT
summary: Turn phase patterns and periodic packets into informative measurement distributions.
why: Provides the explicitly calculated Fourier primitive used in order finding and phase estimation.
advantage: Efficient amplitude transformation; not a direct speedup for producing an explicit classical Fourier vector.

title: Quantum phase estimation
summary: Estimate a unitary eigenphase using controlled powers and an inverse QFT.
why: Central bridge from coherent transformations to numerical estimates.
advantage: Proven precision/confidence guarantees under controlled-unitary access; powered blocks are not free base-U calls.

title: Iterative phase estimation and semiclassical Fourier measurement
summary: Reuse a counting qubit with adaptive corrections and distinguish terminal measurement transformations.
why: Prevents confusing fewer qubits with fewer powered-unitary applications.
advantage: Proven ideal measurement equivalence and width tradeoff; no universal runtime advantage.

title: Period finding and modular order finding
summary: Fourier-sample periodic arithmetic states and reconstruct a candidate denominator.
why: Supplies the quantum subroutine needed by Shor.
advantage: Proven polynomial quantum modular-order algorithm with efficient arithmetic; generic period oracles need separate access promises.

title: Shor’s factoring algorithm
summary: Use a quantum order sample, classical verification and gcds to split a composite integer.
why: Combines all quantum and classical steps and explicitly rejects unsuccessful trials.
advantage: Proven polynomial-time quantum factoring; advantage is against best known classical methods, not a proved classical exponential lower bound.

title: Quantum discrete logarithms
summary: Recover a hidden modular slope using a two-register Fourier transform.
why: Shows a second number-theoretic use of Fourier sampling with a different classical reconstruction.
advantage: Proven polynomial quantum algorithm in efficient group models; classical baseline depends on the group.

title: The abelian hidden-subgroup framework
summary: Unify coset preparation, character cancellation and classical reconstruction.
why: Connects demonstrated Simon, order-finding and discrete-logarithm mechanisms.
advantage: Proven efficient algorithms for suitable finite abelian representations; does not extend automatically to nonabelian HSP.

title: Quantum counting
summary: Infer a marked count from the Grover operator’s eigenphases.
why: Connects search oscillations with numerical estimation.
advantage: Proven oracle-model approximate-counting guarantees; exact and relative counting have different precision costs.

title: Canonical quantum amplitude estimation
summary: Estimate a nonuniform preparation’s good probability by QPE.
why: Provides the probability-estimation primitive for Monte Carlo applications.
advantage: Proven ideal coherent-query precision advantage; preparation, inverse access and readout assumptions remain.

title: Iterative and maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation
summary: Infer amplitudes from multiple Grover depths, with distinct adaptive and likelihood methods.
why: Separates width savings, alias resolution and finite-sample confidence.
advantage: IQAE has rigorous ideal query bounds; the original MLAE analysis has different statistical guarantees and is not a universal confidence theorem.

title: Quantum mean estimation and Monte Carlo
summary: Encode a bounded payoff’s expectation in a flag and estimate it.
why: Makes probability estimation useful while exposing loading, payoff arithmetic and precision costs.
advantage: Proven coherent-query advantages with bounded-output or variance assumptions; practical workload advantage is not established generally.

title: Jordan’s quantum gradient estimation
summary: Encode a local linear function as multidimensional phase ramps.
why: Clarifies the powerful coherent oracle behind a one-query gradient claim.
advantage: Oracle-model query advantage for appropriately smooth finite-precision functions; not a general advantage over automatic differentiation.
